Crosswalk between two frames of a scale

Source: R/map.R
scale_map.Rd

Materialises the from -> atoms -> to route as a table: one row per pair of overlapping units with

scale_map(x, source, target, weight = NULL, by = character(), ...)

Arguments

x

The NestedScale the frames belong to.

source, target

Frame names of x.

weight

Weight column for w. NULL uses the default weight; when the object declares no weights at all, every atom gets weight 1 (an equal split).

by

Extra identifier columns carried through from scale_atom_pairs() (e.g. "year").

...

Passed to scale_atom_pairs().

Value

A data.frame with columns <from>, <to> (NA = uncovered by target), n_from, n_overlap, w, w_from, plus any by columns.

Details

  • n_from – atoms in the source unit (its full set, before any target coverage is considered),

  • n_overlap – atoms the pair shares,

  • w – the weight of the overlap (summed atom weights, chosen weight column), the quantity "weighted_mean" aggregation uses,

  • w_from – the full weight of the source unit; w / w_from is the split share "sum" disaggregation uses.

The two label columns are named by the frames; rows with an NA target label are atoms target does not cover. A crosswalk registered with register_scale_map() is returned as-is instead of being derived.

See also

scale_map_between() for the map between two scales.

Examples

s <- scale_example()
scale_map(s, "class", "group")
#>   class group n_from n_overlap   w w_from
#> 1    G1    G1      2         2 300    300
#> 2    G2    GB      2         2 700    700
#> 3    S1    GB      2         1 500   1100
#> 4    S1    GC      2         1 600   1100
scale_map(s, "sector", "class", weight = "count")
#>   sector class n_from n_overlap   w w_from
#> 1      P    G1      4         2 100    200
#> 2      P    G2      4         2 100    200
#> 3      S    S1      2         2 100    100
